input.question: How do new species arise?
input.ground_truth: Evolution is the very gradual change in genes over time. It isn't that one day an organism gave birth to a human. Rather, it's that over a several thousand year span, creatures stopped being a human ancestor and were instead human. There is no absolute point.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do new species arise?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of different colored LEGO bricks. At first, you have just a few colors. But over a long, long time, some of the bricks get broken or change a little bit when you play with them. Sometimes, a red brick might get a blue spot, or a yellow brick might get a little bigger. If you keep playing and building for many, many years, some of these changed bricks might not fit with the old ones anymore. They become so different that they are like a brand new kind of brick!

That’s kind of how new kinds of animals or plants (which we call “new species”) happen. Over a very long time, little changes happen to animals or plants. Sometimes these changes help them live better in their home. After many, many generations, they can become so different that they are like a new kind of animal or plant—just like the new LEGO brick!
